name: Builders of the Skyline: Architects, Engineers and Styles
description: From Brunelleschi's dome to Zaha Hadid's curves: the architects and engineers who changed how buildings look and stand, the styles they led and the works that made their names.

checkpoints.name: Domes and basilicas
checkpoints.note: Brunelleschi crowns Florence Cathedral with a dome, Michelangelo designs the dome of St. Peter's Basilica and Bernini its colonnade, Palladio designs villas and Sinan builds mosques for the Ottoman sultans. The Baroque fills Europe with drama, Christopher Wren rebuilds St Paul's Cathedral after London's fire, and Versailles shows royal architecture on the largest scale.

checkpoints.name: Iron and steel
checkpoints.note: The Gothic Revival brings back pointed arches, Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace and Brunel's bridges show what iron can do, and Haussmann rebuilds Paris. The Bessemer process makes steel cheap and the elevator makes height usable. After the Great Chicago Fire, Louis Sullivan and the Home Insurance Building begin the skyscraper, and Gustave Eiffel's tower rises over Paris.

checkpoints.name: Masters of modernism
checkpoints.note: Gaudi's Sagrada Familia grows slowly in Barcelona. Walter Gropius founds the Bauhaus, Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe invent a modern style, Frank Lloyd Wright builds Fallingwater over a waterfall, the Chrysler Building brings Art Deco to New York, and Oscar Niemeyer shapes Brasilia in concrete curves.

checkpoints.name: Icons and prizes
checkpoints.note: The Sydney Opera House shows that the shape of a building can become the image of a city. The Pritzker Prize, first given in 1979, honours architects such as I. M. Pei, who adds a glass pyramid to the Louvre in 1989.

checkpoints.name: Any shape at all
checkpoints.note: Frank Gehry and Zaha Hadid use computers to design buildings that curve, fold and lean, and become the best-known architects of their age, with works on every continent.
